description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic featuring tender chicken pieces swimming in a rich, creamy tomato-based gravy. This iconic dish balances sweet and savory notes with aromatic spices, making it a comforting and flavorful meal perfect for any occasion. Its velvety texture and vibrant color promise a delightful culinary experience.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts

ingredients.notes: soaked in hot water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and a pinch of salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned on all sides and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Makhani Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of butter. Reduce heat to medium. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce has thickened. Blend the soaked cashews with a little water until smooth, then add to the tomato mixture.

instructions.title: Finish the Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, crushed fenugreek leaves, and sugar. Add the cooked chicken back into the gravy. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Stir in the heavy cream and 1 tablespoon of butter, ensuring it is well combined. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with a drizzle of extra cream and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For an extra smooth gravy, blend the tomato-onion base with an immersion blender or in a regular blender before adding the chicken and cream.
Adjust the level of spice by increasing or decreasing the red chili powder. For a deeper color without much heat, use Kashmiri red chili powder.
If you dont have fresh ginger garlic paste, you can finely mince fresh ginger and garlic separately. The ratio is typically 1:1.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, is an undeniable superstar of Indian cuisine. This rich, creamy, and mildly spiced dish has captured hearts worldwide, making it a perennial favorite for dinner parties, restaurant outings, and, perhaps most delightfully, a satisfying Indian lunch. Its vibrant orange hue, succulent chicken pieces, and luscious tomato-based gravy make it an irresistible choice, offering a comforting yet exotic culinary experience. If you’re looking to elevate your midday meal, mastering this classic Butter Chicken recipe is a fantastic way to bring the flavors of India right to your table.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant, it was reportedly created by Kundan Lal Jaggi, who combined leftover tandoori chicken with a rich tomato and butter gravy. The dish quickly became a sensation, celebrated for its tender pieces of chicken swimming in a velvety smooth sauce. Key to its distinctive flavor profile are fresh tomatoes (often pureed), copious amounts of butter, a generous swirl of cream, and the aromatic dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Unlike some spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is known for its mild, subtly sweet, and tangy taste, making it incredibly approachable for all palates. It’s a hearty and fulfilling meal, perfect for a warming Indian lunch that leaves you feeling satisfied without being overly heavy.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken involves two main components: the marinated chicken and the rich, flavorful gravy. Here’s what you’ll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, less heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Silky Gravy:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, then drained)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   1 tablespoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed between palms
*   Fresh cilantro for garnish

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Butter Chicken

Follow these steps to create a truly authentic and delicious Murgh Makhani:

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
You have a few options here:
*   **Grill:** Thread chicken onto skewers and grill until cooked through and slightly charred.
*   **Pan-fry:** Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Set aside.
*   **Bake:** Arrange chicken on a baking sheet and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until cooked.

**Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base**
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews, red chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the mixture is thick.

**Step 4: Blend the Gravy**
Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, strain the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on the solids with a spatula to extract all the liquid. Discard any remaining solids.

**Step 5: Finish the Gravy**
Return the smooth gravy to the pot over low-medium heat. Stir in the sugar. Add the remaining butter (about 1-2 tablespoons) and let it melt into the sauce. Pour in the heavy cream and stir gently until fully incorporated. Add the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the gravy to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

**Step 6: Combine and Serve**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Simmer for another 5 minutes to heat the chicken through and allow it to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream just before serving. This homemade Butter Chicken is a fantastic Indian lunch option.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is absolutely possible with a few insider tips:

*   **Marination Time is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is highly recommended.
*   **Charring the Chicken:** A slight char on the chicken pieces before adding them to the gravy adds a wonderful smoky depth that mimics traditional tandoor cooking.
*   **Strain for Silkiness:** Don't skip straining the gravy after blending if you desire that ultra-smooth, restaurant-style texture. It removes any fibrous bits from the onions or tomatoes.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality canned tomatoes (San Marzano if possible) or very ripe fresh ones. Full-fat heavy cream and real butter are non-negotiable for that signature richness.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is quintessential to authentic Butter Chicken. Don't omit it!
*   **Balance Sweet and Tangy:** The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Adjust to your preference, but a touch of sweetness is part of the classic profile.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments. For an authentic Indian lunch experience, serve your Butter Chicken with:

*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for soaking up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan are particularly delightful.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the creamy curry and helps temper its richness.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads like whole wheat roti or flaky paratha also make excellent accompaniments.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip with cucumber or mint can provide a refreshing counterpoint to the warm, spicy (even if mild) curry.
*   **Fresh Salad or Pickled Onions:** A simple side salad with a light vinaigrette or some sliced pickled red onions can add a fresh crunch and cut through the richness.

## Variations & Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is perfect, there are many ways to adapt it to your dietary needs or preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** For a delicious vegetarian twist, replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) to make Paneer Butter Masala, or use firm tofu for a Tofu Butter Masala. Mixed vegetables like peas, carrots, and potatoes can also be used.
*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can substitute some of the cream with Greek yogurt (stirred in at the very end to prevent curdling) or even use coconut milk for a dairy-free alternative, though the flavor profile will change slightly.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the red chili powder to your liking. For more heat, add a finely chopped green chili or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the gravy.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a cashew allergy, you can omit them entirely, though the gravy will be less rich and creamy. Alternatively, you can use melon seeds or poppy seeds (soaked and blended) as a thickener and to add a similar texture.
*   **Pre-made Paste:** For convenience, you can use a good quality store-bought Butter Chicken paste. However, fresh ingredients and homemade spices will always yield the most authentic and flavorful result.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's a culinary journey that promises warmth, comfort, and exquisite flavors. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking for a new challenge, making this iconic Indian lunch recipe from scratch is a rewarding experience that will undoubtedly impress your family and friends. So roll up your sleeves, gather your ingredients, and prepare to indulge in the creamy, dreamy delight of Murgh Makhani!
